subject: Framework version changed after renewal - need explanation ASAP
body:
Hi,

We just noticed that our framework in the platform is showing a completely different version of the standard than what we've been working against for months. All the control numbers are different, some requirements have changed wording or scope, and none of the mapping we'd already done lines up anymore.

We didn't make this change on our end, and nobody told us this was going to happen. Can someone explain why this switched and whether this is expected behavior after a renewal? Right now we're completely stuck - we can't tell which controls we still need evidence for, and our internal notes/mapping docs are all based on the old numbering.

I have to be honest, this is a big deal for us. We have an audit coming up later this year and this kind of surprise change, with zero notice, is exactly the kind of thing that makes us question whether we can rely on this platform. I'm going to need a real answer on how this happened and how we're supposed to handle the transition, because right now I'm having to explain to my leadership why our compliance tracking just got upended without warning.

Please advise as soon as possible - we're blocked until we understand what's going on and how to fix our mapping.

Thanks.

subject: Need answer ASAP - can I run two frameworks at once?
body:
Hi,

I need to know quickly - can I add a second framework (ISO 27001) to my account while I'm already running SOC 2, and have them both active at the same time? Or do I need to finish one before starting the other?

Before I commit to adding it, I want to make sure this won't mess up the evidence I've already collected for SOC 2 or force me to redo/duplicate any of the controls I've already mapped. I don't want to end up having to collect the same evidence twice for overlapping controls between the two frameworks.

I know I could just go through and manually map out the overlapping controls myself if I have to, but that's going to take a lot of extra time and I'd rather not do it that way if the platform can handle it.

Can someone confirm whether this is supported and how it works before I go ahead and add the second framework? Need this answered soon so I can move forward either way.

Thanks

subject: Readiness score stuck at 0% despite completed controls - feature request
body:
I've marked a whole batch of controls as Complete and the readiness score is still showing 0%. This is not the first time I've run into this and it's honestly getting embarrassing when I pull up the dashboard in front of other people and it looks like nothing has been done.

I know the current design apparently doesn't account for controls like this, but that's exactly what I'm asking to get fixed/added. The nightly job that calculates the readiness score should be able to pick up manually added controls automatically instead of just silently ignoring them. Right now it seems like unless a control gets linked to the framework in some specific way, it just doesn't get counted at all, even though it shows as Complete everywhere else in the UI.

I get that I can go in and manually link each control to the framework myself to make it show up in the score, and I've been doing that as a workaround, but with the number of controls we manage that's a real time sink and it shouldn't be necessary. Please build this so newly added controls get tied into the readiness calculation without me having to do it by hand every time.

Would like to know if this is something that's being considered.

subject: URGENT - Shared control mapping not showing between two frameworks
body:
Hi,

Need a quick answer on this if possible, it's a bit time sensitive on my end.

We have two frameworks active in our account and I'd expect a couple of controls that look identical (same wording, same intent) to be mapped/shared between them so we're not managing duplicate evidence for the same thing twice. Instead they're showing up as two completely separate controls with no shared mapping between them.

Is this expected behavior or is something not linking correctly? I know I can go in and manually cross-reference/tag them myself as a workaround, but that's slow and I'd rather not do double the evidence work every cycle if there's a setting or process I'm missing to get them to share a mapping. Can someone confirm whether this is just how it works when you have two frameworks live at once, or if there's something I need to configure?

Separately, while I have you - we've also been struggling with actually implementing and tracking controls in general. It's not always clear what "in progress" vs "implemented" should mean for a given control, and we don't have a great way to see at a glance which controls still need work vs which are done. If there's guidance or a better view for this I'd appreciate pointers, since we're trying to get organized this quarter.

Would appreciate a fast reply on at least the mapping question since we're trying to plan our workload around it. Thanks!

subject: Framework version changed on its own - control numbers don't match anymore
body:
We logged in today to prep for our audit and noticed our whole framework has switched to a different version of the standard than what we've been working from all year. All the control numbers and requirements are different now, and none of the evidence we mapped previously lines up with the new structure.

Nobody told us this was going to happen. We didn't request a change and there was no notice in the platform that this was coming. Our auditor is expecting us to walk through the controls we originally set up, and now none of it matches.

Can someone explain how/why this happened and whether this is expected behavior when a plan renews? Is there a way to see which version we're supposed to be on, or revert back to what we had before? We are up against a hard deadline with our auditor and can't move forward until this is sorted out. This has already cost us hours today just trying to figure out what changed.

Please advise ASAP.

subject: URGENT - Need ability to run two frameworks at the same time
body:
Hi,

I need to know if it's possible (or if it can be added) to run two compliance frameworks at once in the platform, like SOC 2 and ISO 27001 together. Right now it looks like I'd have to pick one framework and fully set it up before starting on the other, which means duplicating a lot of work for controls that overlap between the two.

This is urgent - I need an answer quickly because I have to decide how to structure our compliance program and can't keep going back and forth manually collecting the same evidence twice for controls that clearly overlap between frameworks.

Can you please add support for running multiple frameworks simultaneously, or at least let me know if this is something on your roadmap? I really need a fast response on this so I can plan accordingly.

Thanks

subject: URGENT: Readiness score stuck at 0% despite controls marked Complete
body:
We have a batch of controls that we added manually and marked as Complete, but our overall readiness score is still showing 0%. This has been the case since we added them and the nightly refresh hasn't fixed it either.

This is urgent - we have an audit coming up in a few months and need our dashboard to actually reflect our real progress for internal reporting and for our team's peace of mind. Right now it looks like we've done zero work even though these controls are all done.

I can go in and manually check things but that's not really sustainable if the score never updates on its own - can someone look into why these completed controls aren't being counted toward the readiness score? Please let me know what's going on and how to fix this ASAP.

subject: Wrong company name on invoices - where do I update this?
body:
Hi,

I noticed our invoices are showing the wrong legal company name. I looked through account settings and billing settings but couldn't find a field to correct it myself.

Could you let me know where this is normally updated, or if it has to be changed on your end? Just want to understand how this is supposed to work before our next billing cycle.

Thanks,

subject: Need to reuse ISO 27001 scoping for SOC 2 - urgent question
body:
Hi,

We already completed all of our scoping work for ISO 27001 outside of your platform (asset inventory, boundaries, applicable controls, etc.) and now we're trying to set up SOC 2 in the platform. It looks like we have to start the scoping process completely from scratch for SOC 2 even though a lot of it overlaps with what we already did for ISO 27001.

Is there a way to bring that existing scoping information over or apply it to the new framework so we don't have to redo all of it? We're completely stuck on moving forward with SOC 2 setup until we know how to handle this, so I'd really appreciate a fast answer.

Thanks

subject: Wrong legal entity name on our certificate - needs to be fixed ASAP
body:
The company name printed on our framework certificate does not match our actual legal entity name, and I cannot find any setting in the account to correct this myself. I've dug through the org settings and profile pages and there's nothing that lets me update it.

This needs to be fixed on your end. We have an audit coming up later this year and we cannot show up with a certificate that has the wrong legal entity name on it - that's not something our auditors or our leadership will accept.

Honestly, this is the kind of basic thing that makes me question whether we should keep using this platform. We're paying for this to be handled correctly and instead I'm stuck chasing down a support ticket to fix something that should be editable from our end in the first place.

Please correct the legal entity name and reissue the certificate. If there's a manual process on your side to fix this, that's fine, but I need confirmation it's being done and a timeline for when we'll have the corrected version.

subject: Feature request: readiness score doesn't account for auditor findings
body:
We're currently in fieldwork with our auditor and our framework dashboard shows 100% readiness, but the auditor has already flagged several gaps in controls that the platform is marking as fully ready. This is causing some confusion internally since we were relying on that 100% number to tell leadership we were in good shape, and now we're scrambling to reconcile the auditor's findings against what the tool is showing.

I understand for now we can just manually track the auditor's findings in a spreadsheet alongside the platform, but that's slow and means keeping two systems in sync during an active audit, which isn't ideal.

What I'd like to request is some way for the readiness score to actually incorporate auditor feedback/findings - like a way to log gaps the auditor identifies and have that adjust the readiness percentage or at least flag those specific controls as "under review" or "flagged by auditor" instead of showing green/100% when there are known open issues. Right now there's a disconnect between what the dashboard says and what's actually happening in fieldwork, and since we're mid-audit this is becoming a real problem for reporting status accurately to stakeholders.

Can this be added, or is there a timeline for something like this being built?

subject: Can't view GDPR control set without adding the framework first - blocking us
body:
This is causing a real problem for us. We're trying to figure out if the GDPR framework is even the right fit before we commit to adding it to our account, but there's no way to actually see the control set first. The only option is to add the framework outright, which isn't something we want to do blind.

We have an audit coming up very soon and need to finalize which controls we're mapping to ASAP, but we can't make that decision without seeing what's actually in the GDPR set. This is holding up our whole prep process and there's no workaround that I can find - I've looked everywhere in the settings and framework pages.

Can you please fix this so we can preview a framework's controls before adding it? Having to commit first just to see what we're getting into makes no sense and is costing us time we don't have right now. Please treat this urgently, our audit timeline is tight.

subject: Feature request: reuse ISO 27001 scoping for SOC 2 setup
body:
We already completed scoping for ISO 27001 in a separate process outside of your platform before we started using it, and now that we're setting up SOC 2 in the platform, it's asking us to go through the entire scoping process again from scratch.

A lot of this overlaps - systems, boundaries, in-scope processes, etc. are largely the same between the two frameworks. It would be great if there was a way to import or map that existing scoping work into a new framework setup so we're not duplicating effort every time we add a framework.

Right now the only option is to manually re-enter everything, which is slow and we're on a tight timeline - our audit is coming up soon and this is eating into the time we have to actually prepare for it. We can do the manual entry if we have to, but wanted to flag this as something that should really be built in, since I'd assume other customers running multiple frameworks hit the same issue.

Can you pass this along as a feature request?

subject: Certificate shows wrong company name - need a way to fix this
body:
The legal entity name on our issued certificate does not match our actual registered legal entity name, and I cannot find anywhere in the platform to correct this myself. I've gone through account settings, org profile, and the certificate/framework pages and there's simply no option to edit or update the name that appears on the certificate.

This isn't a small typo issue for us - a certificate with the wrong legal name is not something we can hand to clients or partners as proof of compliance. Right now we're stuck with a document that's effectively unusable and no self-serve way to correct it.

I'm submitting this as a feature request: please add the ability for account admins to edit/correct the legal entity name tied to a certificate and have it regenerate correctly. This seems like a pretty basic requirement for a compliance platform and its absence is honestly making us question whether this tool is fit for purpose.

We're currently blocked on this with no workaround, and I want to be upfront - my team is already discussing whether we need to look at other platforms if this can't be resolved. Please let me know if this is something that's being addressed, and on what timeline, because I need to bring an update back to my leadership.

subject: Urgent - Readiness score shows 100% but auditor is finding gaps?
body:
Hi,

We need clarification on this ASAP because our team is stuck and can't move forward.

Our dashboard shows our framework at 100% ready - all controls green, no outstanding items flagged anywhere. But our auditor is going through fieldwork right now and has already found several gaps in controls that the platform is showing as fully complete.

This doesn't make sense to us. If the readiness score says 100%, shouldn't that mean the controls are actually solid and would hold up to an auditor's review? What exactly does the 100% score mean if it's not catching things an auditor considers a gap?

We need to understand how this score is calculated and why it isn't lining up with what our auditor is finding, so we can figure out how to close whatever we're missing. Please respond quickly, this is blocking us and we don't have a workaround in the meantime.

Thanks,

subject: Urgent: Need to preview GDPR control set before adding framework
body:
Hi,

We're trying to evaluate whether the GDPR framework is the right fit for us, but I can't find any way to see what controls are actually included in that set without first adding the framework to our account.

Is there a way to preview or view the full GDPR control list before committing to add it? We don't want to add a framework and have it show up across our account/dashboards if we're not sure yet it's the right one.

This is blocking us right now and I need an answer quickly - can someone confirm if this is possible and how, or if there's a reason this isn't available?

Thanks,

subject: Scoping work from ISO 27001 not carrying over to SOC 2
body:
We already went through the whole scoping exercise for ISO 27001 last year - documented our systems, data flows, in-scope processes, all of it - but we did that work outside your platform before we onboarded. Now that we're setting up SOC 2 in the platform, it's asking us to go through scoping again from scratch as if none of that exists.

Is there a way to import or reference the scoping work we already did so it counts toward SOC 2 as well? Seems like a lot of overlap between the two frameworks and it's frustrating to have to redo hours of work that's already been done just because it wasn't originally entered here.

We do have an audit coming up down the line, so I'd rather not spend time manually re-entering everything if there's a smarter way to link it up. If there isn't, just let me know and I'll have someone start re-keying it in manually, but wanted to check first since this is costing us time we don't really have to spare.

subject: Feature Request: Ability to correct company name on issued certificate - blocking us
body:
We just pulled our framework certificate and the company name printed on it doesn't match our actual legal entity name. I've gone through every settings page I can find in the account and there is no way to edit or correct this myself. This isn't a small typo issue - a certificate with the wrong legal entity name is essentially useless to us for anything official (vendor reviews, contracts, etc.).

I need this to be a self-serve fix, not something that requires me to open a support ticket every time. Right now there's simply no option anywhere in the product to update the entity name and regenerate the certificate, and that's a real gap for a platform whose whole purpose is producing compliance documentation that's supposed to be accurate.

To be blunt, this is putting our decision to keep using this platform at risk. We're actively being asked by our leadership why our compliance certificate has the wrong company name on it, and I don't have a good answer other than "the vendor doesn't support fixing that." We are blocked from using this certificate until it's corrected, and I don't have a workaround.

Please treat this as a feature request to add a way for account admins to update the legal entity name on file and have it reflected on any issued certificates. I need to know if this is something you're planning to build, and on what timeline, because we're evaluating other options if this can't be resolved.

subject: Need to see whether a control is automated or manual - not shown anywhere
body:
This is honestly costing me way more time than it should. As a control owner, I have no way of telling from a control's page whether it's automated (tested via some integration sync) or manual (needs me to upload evidence myself). There's just nothing on the page that says which one it is.

I ended up wasting a bunch of time manually uploading evidence for a control that I later found out was already being tested automatically, and on other controls I assumed something was being handled automatically when it actually wasn't - so evidence just never got uploaded. Both situations made me look like I dropped the ball when really I just had no way of knowing what was expected.

We have an audit coming up in a few months and I really don't want to be scrambling to figure this out control-by-control right before then.

Can you please add a label or indicator on each control's page that clearly shows whether it's automated or manual? This seems like pretty basic info that should be visible, and right now there's no way for me to find it in the product at all. Please build this in - it's a real blocker for us managing our controls properly.

subject: URGENT - Can I mark a control as not applicable?
body:
Hi,

I need to know quickly - is there a way to mark a control as "Not Applicable" so it stops counting against our readiness score? Please let me know ASAP if this feature exists and where to find it, or if there's some other way to handle controls that don't apply to us.

Thanks

subject: URGENT: Bug - Can't tell which controls are automated vs manual
body:
This needs to be looked at ASAP. I'm going through our controls list and I can't figure out which ones are supposed to be automated (synced automatically) and which ones need me to manually upload evidence. The control page itself doesn't say anything - there's no label, no icon, nothing indicating the type.

I've had controls that I assumed would just update on their own but never did, and I only find out after waiting around wondering why no evidence showed up. This is really confusing and wasting a lot of my time trying to guess.

subject: Is it possible to mark a control as not applicable?
body:
Hi, need a quick answer on this - we have a few controls in our readiness score that just don't apply to us, and they're dragging our percentage down. Is there a way to mark a control as "not applicable" so it doesn't count against us?

subject: Bug: No way to tell if a control is automated or manual - this is a real problem
body:
I keep running into this and it's honestly making me question whether we should stick with this platform.

When I open a control page, there is absolutely nothing telling me whether that control is supposed to be tested automatically or if I need to manually upload evidence for it. I've had multiple owners on my team ask me "do I need to do anything here or is this handled automatically?" and I don't have a good answer because the control page itself doesn't say.

This isn't a one-off - it's happening across basically every control we have set up. Right now the only "workaround" is for someone to just guess, upload evidence anyway just in case, and hope that's the right call, which is obviously not sustainable and wastes a ton of time for something that should just be labeled clearly on the page.

Can you please fix this? We need to know, right on the control itself, whether it's automated (via integration sync or whatever) or manual (needs evidence uploaded). Otherwise I genuinely don't know how anyone is supposed to trust the compliance status you're showing us. If this isn't something that can be addressed soon, we're going to have to seriously look at other tools, because my team is losing confidence in this one.

subject: Can I mark a control as not applicable?
body:

subject: Feature request: show whether a control is automated or manual on the control page
body:
Our auditor is starting review this week and I keep running into the same issue while going through our controls list - there's no way to tell from a control's own page whether it's supposed to be tested automatically (via an integration sync) or if it needs someone to manually upload evidence for it.

Could you add a label or indicator directly on the control page that shows whether it's automated or manual? That way owners can immediately know what they need to do (wait for the sync vs. upload evidence themselves) without having to ask around or dig through settings. This would really help us move faster right now and would be useful long-term too.

Thanks.

body:

subject: Need bulk status update for controls - clicking through each one is a huge time sink
body:
This has been bugging me for a while and I finally have to say something. There's no way to select multiple controls and update their status at once - I have to click into every single control individually, change the status, save, go back, and repeat.

After our last review I had to update status on a few dozen controls and it ate up my entire afternoon. That's insane for what should be a simple bulk action. I know I can just keep doing it one by one manually, but that's not a real solution when you're dealing with more than a handful of controls at a time.

Can you please add a way to multi-select controls and change their status in bulk? Even just a checkbox next to each control with a "update status" button for the selected ones would fix this. This feels like a pretty basic feature that's missing and it's costing me real time every time I have to do a batch update.

subject: No notification when control ownership is reassigned
body:
Hi,

Please let me know what's needed to get this turned on.

Thanks

subject: Shared control description not syncing across frameworks - is this expected?
body:
I need clarity on this ASAP because it's blocking me right now.

We have a control that's mapped to both SOC 2 and ISO 27001. I updated the description on that control while I had it open under SOC 2, expecting it to update everywhere since it's the same shared control. If it's a bug, please let me know how quickly it can be fixed because right now I have no way around it.

subject: Bug: Controls showing "Pass" even when automated test hasn't run in weeks
body:
This is a serious issue and it's actively causing problems for us right now with our auditor breathing down our neck.

We have several controls that rely on automated tests, and I just discovered that a few of them are showing a "Pass" status even though the underlying test hasn't actually run in over 30 days. As far as I can tell there's nowhere in the settings to make a control automatically flip to "Fail" (or at least "Stale"/"Needs attention") if its test hasn't executed recently, regardless of what the last recorded result was.

This is a huge problem because it means we could be sitting on stale "Pass" statuses for controls that may no longer even be functioning, and we have no way to catch that other than manually checking every single control's last run date ourselves. That's not scalable and it completely defeats the purpose of automated testing if the platform will just keep showing green even when nothing has run in weeks.

I need this fixed ASAP - our audit is happening very soon and I cannot walk in with controls showing "Pass" that are actually just stale data. Please tell me how to configure an auto-fail rule based on test recency, or if this genuinely isn't possible right now, I need to know that immediately so I can figure out another way to handle this before the audit.

This is blocking us and there's no workaround I've found. Please escalate.

subject: Notes field on controls overwrites previous entries - no version history
body:
This is a pretty serious issue. My teammate had written detailed notes on one of our controls explaining the evidence and context for our auditor, and I went in today to add my own comment and it just completely wiped out what she had written. There's no history, no previous versions, nothing - it just shows my latest text like her notes never existed.

I only realized this after the fact, so now we've lost that context entirely and I have to ask her to try to remember what she wrote and redo it. This is exactly the kind of thing that makes us look unorganized in front of an auditor, and we do have an audit coming up later this year, so losing this kind of documentation is not something we can afford to keep happening.

Right now the only way around it is to have people copy/paste their notes somewhere else before anyone else edits the field, which is obviously not a real solution and just adds extra manual work for something the tool should be handling on its own.

Can you please fix this so that edits to the notes field don't just overwrite what someone else wrote? At minimum there should be some kind of version history or log of changes so we're not losing work every time two people touch the same control. This seems like a basic feature for a compliance tool where documentation history actually matters.

subject: URGENT: No evidence guidance for custom controls - audit blocked
body:
Hi team,

We're in the middle of prepping for our audit (auditor is already asking for evidence) and we've hit a real problem with the custom controls we wrote ourselves.

For every template control in the platform, there's clear guidance on what evidence would actually satisfy it - great, no issues there. But for any control we authored ourselves, there's nothing. No suggestions, no examples, nothing telling us what kind of evidence would be acceptable. We're basically guessing at what to upload and hoping it lines up with what the auditor expects.

I know this isn't something that exists today, but we really need this built in - some kind of guidance or evidence recommendation for custom controls, similar to what template controls already have. Right now we're stuck manually figuring out and documenting evidence requirements ourselves for every custom control, which is slow and error-prone, and we don't have a lot of time to spare with the audit clock already running.

Can someone escalate this as a feature request? We need a fast response given the timing - even a rough version of this (like letting us define/attach expected evidence criteria to a custom control) would help a ton.

Thanks,

subject: URGENT: Need ability to assign two owners to a single control
body:
Hi,

Sam
